text:
B: Hi, can you hear me?
A: Hi, yeah. Sorry, I'm Harriet.
B: Kerry. Nice to meet you.
A: You too.
B: So where are you based?
A: Erm, Walthamstow. In London. I'm a student, I'm in my final year at Queen Mary, doing history.
B: Oh, right. I did think you might be a teacher or something, with all the books behind you.
A: [laughs] No, that's just, I work in a secondhand bookshop, so they sort of follow me home.
B: Yeah. So, what's the plan after? Will you teach?
A: Erm. I don't know, honestly. My mum keeps suggesting it, she's a deputy head. I've half thought about archives, maybe a master's. I haven't actually looked at any deadlines, though. I just say I'm going to.
B: Oh, there's loads of time.
A: Maybe. What about you, what do you do?
B: I'm a service advisor at a car dealership near Cheltenham. Senior. So booking people in for services and repairs, explaining the work, selling service plans.
A: Oh, okay. Do you have to deal with a lot of, I don't know, people who are cross?
B: Yeah, every day. You get used to it. You just stay calm, explain it nicely, and most of them come round.
A: I think I'd be terrible at that. At the shop people bring things in and ask what they're worth, and I'm just like, erm, sorry, about fifty p.
B: [laughs] Yeah, you'd not be on commission, then.
A: No. Definitely not.
B: Do you live on your own up there?
A: No, with my boyfriend, Callum. It's a flat above a nail bar. So the stairs smell of acetone, constantly.
B: Oh, that'd be handy, though. I need mine doing, look.
A: [laughs] Yeah, I've never actually been in. Which is probably a bit weird.
B: Just pop down. Do you two cook, or?
A: He does, mostly. He's got a sourdough starter that he's named. I do pasta bakes and toast.
B: Pasta bake's a staple in ours, the kids love it. That and fajitas.
A: How old are your kids?
B: Eleven and eight. Isla and Jacob. And the dog, Biscuit.
A: Oh, the one in the photo. He looked very settled.
B: He's settled now. He's not settled when he's eating the skirting boards. [laughs]
A: Erm. Sorry, I've gone blank. Do you get much time off, with work and the kids?
B: Not really, no. One Saturday in four I'm in. We have a holiday every year, though, that's the thing we save for. Lanzarote, probably, next summer, all-inclusive.
A: That sounds nice. We went to Lisbon last summer and it was lovely, we just sort of walked round for a week and ate pastries.
B: Yeah, I'm not really a walking round person, I'm more by the pool. I'd want a kids' club, honestly, otherwise it's not a holiday, is it?
A: No, that's fair. I mean, I'd probably just read by the pool anyway.
B: See, that's the dream. Book, pool, pink gin.
A: I could do the book bit, I think. I'd bring about three and not finish
